C1-01-levels-ecological-organisation

A vertical "ladder" or set of nested boxes showing the levels of ecological organisation from smallest to largest. Six panels, each a little larger than the one before: (1) a single Tilapia fish; (2) a small school of Tilapia fish; (3) a pond scene with Tilapia, water lilies, a frog, a dragonfly and floating algae; (4) the same pond with the sun, water, mud and air shown around it; (5) a wide landscape of tropical rainforest; (6) the globe of the Earth. Arrows connect each panel to the next. Soft greens and blues.
C1-02-ecological-tolerance-curve-graph

A simple bell-shaped graph showing the range of tolerance of an organism for one environmental factor. The horizontal axis is the factor (for example temperature, from low to high); the vertical axis is the number of organisms (or growth). The curve is low at both ends and high in the middle. Shade the central high part as the optimum zone, the parts on each side as zones of stress, and the two ends where the curve meets the axis as zones of intolerance (no organisms). Soft green curve, pale yellow and pale red shading.
C1-04-altitudinal-zonation-mountain

Side view of a mountain rising from a hot lowland plain on the left to a cool plateau top on the right, showing how vegetation changes with altitude. At the foot: tall lowland forest or savanna trees with a thermometer showing a high reading. Halfway up: denser, shorter montane forest with mist. At the top: open montane grassland with grazing cattle, a tea bush and a potato plant, and a thermometer showing a lower reading. A vertical arrow on the left side pointing upwards. Soft greens and browns with pale blue sky.
C1-05-soil-structure-comparison

Three cut-away blocks of soil side by side, each showing particles, water and air spaces. Left: sandy soil with large rounded particles, large air spaces and water draining away downwards, with a millet plant on top. Middle: loamy soil with mixed particle sizes, dark humus pieces, an earthworm and a healthy maize plant on top. Right: clay soil with very small tightly packed particles, a layer of standing water on top and a rice plant. Soft browns, tans and greys with blue water.
C1-06-secchi-disc-turbidity-measurement

A person kneeling on a small wooden jetty over a pond, lowering a Secchi disc on a marked rope into green-brown water. Show a cut-away side view of the water: the round disc with four alternating black and white quarters, a small weight underneath, sinking down; the disc fades as it goes deeper. A ruler-style scale along the rope. Two dotted horizontal lines in the water, one where the disc disappears on lowering and one slightly higher where it reappears on raising. Soft blues, greens and browns.
C1-07-six-thermometer-apparatus

Front view of a U-shaped maximum and minimum (Six's) thermometer mounted on a white backing board. Left limb with a completely full alcohol bulb at the top; right limb with a partly filled bulb at the top with a vapour space. A silver mercury thread fills the bottom of the U-bend. A small dark steel index rests above the mercury in each limb. A scale beside each limb (the minimum scale numbers increase downwards; the maximum scale numbers increase upwards). A small horseshoe magnet beside the thermometer. Soft blue alcohol, silver mercury, grey board.
C1-08-rain-gauge-apparatus

Cut-away side view of a standard rain gauge set in the ground in an open grassy area, with rain falling. Show the outer metal cylinder with part of it below ground, a funnel at the top with its rim level, rain drops entering the funnel and running down into a glass collecting bottle inside. Beside the gauge, a separate tall measuring cylinder marked in millimetres, with collected water in it. Grey metal, pale blue water, green grass.
C1-09-hygrometer-apparatus

Front view of a wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer: two identical thermometers mounted side by side on a white board. The right thermometer's bulb is wrapped in white muslin whose tail dips into a small container of water below. The left thermometer shows a higher reading than the right. Small curved lines rising from the muslin to show evaporation. Soft blues and greys.
C1-10-wind-vane-anemometer

A wind vane and a cup anemometer standing side by side on poles on top of a building, against a white background. The wind vane has an arrowhead, a broad tail fin and fixed compass arms marked N, S, E and W below. The cup anemometer has three cups on horizontal arms spinning on a vertical spindle with a small box (counter) at the base. Small curved lines show the wind blowing from the left. Soft greys and blues.
C1-11-ecological-measurement-instruments-set

A neat set of five ecological instruments arranged in a row on a white background: (1) a pH meter with a probe dipped in a beaker of water and a strip of universal indicator paper with a colour chart; (2) a handheld light meter with a dial; (3) a glass hydrometer floating in a tall cylinder of water; (4) a soil auger with a T-shaped handle and a spiral bit, with a core of soil beside it; (5) a barometer with a round dial. Soft greys, blues and browns.
C1-12-soil-drainage-experiment-apparatus

Three identical funnels side by side, each plugged with cotton wool and resting in a measuring cylinder. The left funnel holds pale yellow sandy soil, the middle one dark brown loamy soil, the right one grey-brown clay soil. Water is being poured into each. Below, the cylinders contain different volumes of drained water: the most under the sandy soil, a moderate amount under the loam and the least under the clay. Soft yellows, browns and blues.
C1-13-human-impact-ecosystems

A single landscape scene divided into panels showing human activities that change the distribution of organisms in Nigeria: (1) a cleared forest with tree stumps and a log truck; (2) bush burning in dry savanna grass with smoke and birds flying away; (3) a large flat farm of one crop with a tractor spraying chemicals; (4) a city with buildings and a road cutting through bush; (5) a dam across a river with a large lake behind it; (6) an oil spill in a mangrove creek with dead fish and an oil-coated bird, and a gas flare in the background; (7) bare, trampled land with too many cattle and goats; (8) a hunter carrying bushmeat. Soft natural colours.
C1-03-nigeria-rainfall-vegetation-map

A simple outline map of Nigeria with rainfall shown by colour bands running roughly east to west: dark blue along the southern coast and the Niger Delta (highest rainfall), then lighter blue, pale green, pale yellow, and pale orange-brown in the far north and north-east (lowest rainfall). A wide arrow down the side pointing from south to north. Small icons: rainforest trees and cocoa pods in the south, yam and cassava in the middle belt, millet heads and groundnut plants in the north, and a camel in the far north-east. Soft blues to soft browns.
